title: Caper-Butter Cod Foil Packets
seoTitle: Caper-Butter Cod Foil Packets | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Cod packet night—lemon-caper butter, shaved fennel, and vermouth steam on the grill
subtitle: Foil-packet cod with lemon, capers, fennel, and vermouth butter for the crew
description: Cod portions sealed over shaved fennel with butter, capers, picholine olives, lemon, tarragon, and a splash of dry vermouth, grilled at a steady 400°F to 145°F and opened at the table for the steam.
equipment: Gas or charcoal grill with a lid

steps.title: Shave the fennel and stage the foil
steps.instruction: Slice the fennel bulbs as thin as you can manage — thick fennel stays crunchy-raw in the short packet steam. Slice the lemons into thin rounds and flick out the seeds, drain the capers, halve the picholine olives, and chop the tarragon. Tear 8 double-layer sheets of heavy foil, about 18 inches each; a single layer tears on the grates and dumps the butter into the fire.

steps.title: Dry and season the cod
steps.instruction: Pat every cod portion bone dry with paper towels — surface water dilutes the caper butter into dishwater. Season both sides with the Maldon salt and white pepper. White pepper seasons clean with no black specks against the white flesh, which matters when the packet opens at the table.

steps.title: Build and crimp the packets
steps.instruction: Bed each foil sheet with a handful of shaved fennel, set a cod portion on top, then add a butter pat, a spoonful of capers and olives, two lemon rounds, a pinch of tarragon, and a splash of dry vermouth. Fold and double-crimp every seam tight. The fennel bed lifts the fillet off the hot foil so the bottom steams instead of scorching, and the vermouth becomes the steam that does the cooking.

steps.title: Heat the grill to a steady 400°F
steps.instruction: Preheat the grill to medium, 400°F, lid down, and let it settle 8 minutes so the heat is even across the grates. Packets want steady, moderate heat — a raging grate boils the butter over and scorches the fennel through the foil before the center cooks.

steps.title: Grill the packets until they puff
steps.instruction: Set the packets on the grates seam-side up, close the lid, and give them 12–14 minutes without flipping. They're close when they puff like pillows and you can hear butter sizzling inside. Cod is finished at 145°F — probe straight through the foil at the thickest point with an instant-read.

steps.title: Open a test packet
steps.instruction: Open one packet away from your face — the steam exits fast and hot. The flesh should flake into big white petals at 145°F with the butter bubbling around it. If the center is still translucent, re-crimp that packet and give the whole batch 2 more minutes before checking again.

steps.title: Toast the baguettes on the cool edge
steps.instruction: Halve the crusty baguettes lengthwise and set them cut-side down over the cooler edge of the grates for 1–2 minutes until golden. This is the butter mop — the lemon-caper juice pooled in each packet is the best bite of the night, and the crew will fight over it.

steps.title: Open at the table, finish with dill
steps.instruction: Carry the sealed packets to the table on sheet pans and open them there for the steam and the smell — steer the first blast away from faces. Scatter the fresh dill fronds over each portion and spoon the caper butter back over the flesh. Baguette goes out alongside for dunking.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover sealed cod packets — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool cod and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Double-crimp every seam — one leaky fold and that packet steams dry instead of poaching in butter.
Buy even-thickness cod portions or fold thin tails under so every packet finishes at the same time.
Packets hold sealed at 140°F for about 15 minutes; past that the fillets overcook in their own heat.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Log hold times on the pan with a grease pencil when tones drop mid-service.
Spot-check proteins with an instant-read thermometer before reopening the line after a call.

Condiments: extra lemon wedges, hot sauce for the heat-seekers
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.

leftovers: Cool cod in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.

Flake leftover cod into chowder or fish cakes, and save the packet butter — that's the flavor base.
Reheat gently, covered, with a splash of water; a hard blast turns cod to rubber.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Every firefighter gets a sealed packet that opens in a cloud of lemon-caper steam, and the cleanup is a ball of foil — the rare fish night with zero pans to scrub.
mealPrepNotes: Build and crimp the packets up to 4 hours ahead and refrigerate on sheet pans. Grill at a steady 400°F for 12–14 minutes to 145°F. Hold sealed at 140°F up to 15 minutes; open at the table.
substitutions: Haddock or halibut swaps for cod portion-for-portion — halibut runs a minute or two longer in the packet.
Dry white wine works 1:1 for the vermouth; for no alcohol, use chicken broth plus an extra squeeze of lemon.
Kalamata olives stand in for picholine — stronger and saltier, so use a little less.
No tarragon? Fresh thyme sprigs hold up in the steam; just pull the stems before serving.
